Continue building Trueup in this repository. Read README.md, hackathon.md, CHANGELOG.md and src/ first. This session is recorded by Entire and published: work only inside this repository and never mention anything outside it. Do not git commit or push. Memory is limited: one library at a time.

Task: the checker (false-alarm control) and the deduper. A lead becomes a "finding" only if every checker rule passes; otherwise it is "withdrawn" with the rule that failed. Withdrawn leads are kept and counted, never deleted.

Checker rules (each a pure function over recorded data, with unit tests; the effects that gather the data live outside core):
1. Reproduces in a fresh process, twice, with the same result.
2. Reproduces on the library's recommended setup with the framework package installed.
3. Reproduces on the latest release and on the library's main branch (install the instrumentation packages from a shallow clone of main into a separate venv `.trueup/venvs/<lib>-main`; neatlogs: github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs, OpenInference: github.com/Arize-ai/openinference, OpenLLMetry: github.com/traceloop/openllmetry). If main can't be installed, the rule reports "could not check" with the reason, and the lead stays a lead (not a finding) unless every other rule passes and the reason is recorded.
4. The fake sent what truth claims (usage present when tokens are compared; unique response ids per call).
5. No shared async client across event loops; no export to a dead endpoint.
6. A second library on the same scenario shows the correct behaviour, or the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions define it. If all libraries agree and there is no reference, the lead is marked "disputed semantics", not a finding.
7. A minimal repro under 40 lines that runs with no keys exists (generate it from the scenario; run it to prove it reproduces).

Also: the neatlogs adapter may be producing false leads for finish reason (neatlogs spans carry OpenInference's `llm.finish_reason` but the adapter reads only `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason`). Look at the real spans, decide from evidence, fix the adapter if it is wrong, and record in hackathon.md which leads that removed and why. That is an honest example of Trueup catching its own false alarm; keep the before and after counts.

Dedupe (`src/trueup/dedupe.py`): for each finding, search the library's GitHub issues and PRs (all states) with `gh search issues/prs` using keywords from the finding, list the integration's issue titles, and record the searches with dates. If an existing issue/PR covers it, mark "already known" with the link. Never open, comment or post anything; read only.

Group leads that share a cause (same library, same check, same code path) into one finding with a list of scenarios, so the report is not 50 near-duplicates.

CLI: `trueup check <run_id|latest> [--library x]` runs the checker and dedupe over a sweep's leads and writes `findings.json` and `withdrawn.json`, printing a summary table (findings by severity, withdrawn by rule, already-known). Run it for all three libraries, one at a time, and write the results to hackathon.md (counts and short plain descriptions; no claim beyond the evidence).

Update CHANGELOG.md. Plain words, no filler. `uv run pytest -q` must pass. Finish with a summary: tests, findings per library, withdrawn by rule, already-known with links, and anything not done.
I'll start by reading the project docs and source.

result.output:
Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

`trueup doctor`, `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>` and `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>` work.

`sweep` runs the scenarios (plain SDK, LangChain/LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK; pick with `--framework`) against a fake provider, compares truth with the trace, prints a table of leads and writes truth, trace and `leads.json` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace; it is not a confirmed bug.

`audit` runs your script's `main()` against the fake (through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) under the chosen library, once per fake scenario on each provider route the script calls, and compares the same way. It needs a `main()` with no arguments that uses the `openai` or `anthropic` SDK; see `src/trueup/audit.py` for its limits.

The other commands (`fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no leads, 1 leads found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q         # offline unit tests
uv run pytest -q -m e2e  # builds per-library venvs, runs subprocesses
uv run trueup sweep neatlogs
uv run trueup sweep openllmetry --framework openai-agents
uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library openinference
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
# Build log

neatHack, 10-12 Oct 2026.

## 2026-10-10: skeleton

- Set up the uv project (Python 3.12, src layout) with the `trueup` command.
- Added the data model in `trueup.core`: Observation, Mismatch, Run, Finding and Severity, each with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.
- Nothing is audited yet. No findings so far.

## 2026-10-10: the truth side

- `trueup.fake`: a local fake provider (stdlib http.server in a thread, random free port). It speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. The request's model name picks the scenario: plain, streamed with and without usage, two parallel tool calls with split streamed arguments, refusal, n=2, HTTP 500 and 529, error event mid-stream, status failed and incomplete, reasoning summary, thinking, tool_use with input_json_delta, and a dropped connection. Every id is unique per call and per fake instance. The truth log records each request and what was sent back, including tokens per call, or that no usage was sent.
- 34 fixture tests run the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs against the fake. Two SDK behaviours we found and recorded: the openai SDK passes a Responses `error` event to the app instead of raising, and the anthropic SDK lets a dropped stream through as a raw `RemoteProtocolError`, not an SDK exception.
- `trueup.scenarios`: 31 plain-SDK scenarios as data (chat 12, Responses 9, Anthropic 10), each with expected truth. A unit test runs every app with no tracing library and checks the expectations against what really happens. That check caught one wrong expectation (streamed tool calls without include_usage carry no tokens). 20 LangChain/LangGraph/OpenAI Agents cases are listed as not_built.
- `trueup.runner`: runs one scenario in a fresh subprocess in `.trueup/venvs/<lib>` (built with uv), using the library's recommended setup and an in-memory span exporter. It returns truth plus spans as JSON. A scenario that cannot run is reported NOT RUN with the reason.
- Regression tests for four traps: reused response ids, a reused async client across asyncio.run, a missing-usage reply read as a bug, and neatlogs exporting to a dead endpoint.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations and `summary.txt` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. All three libraries ran 31/31. The first openllmetry sweep was 0/31 NOT RUN because `traceloop-sdk` imports `httpx` without declaring it; we now install `httpx` in that venv.
- Leads for the comparer (not judged yet): neatlogs adds `stream_options.include_usage` to the app's streamed chat request. openinference exports no span for a stream closed early, or for a Responses stream that ends with an error event. openllmetry marks chat streams that raised (error event, cut) as OK, and exports no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream errors and cuts.

## 2026-10-10: the comparer and the reports

- `trueup.core.compare` checks truth against the spans: run status, call status, call count, span closed, tokens, output (text, refusal, tool calls with arguments compared as JSON), finish, plus a "request changed" note. Severity: HIGH changes a number or status a dashboard shows by default, MEDIUM is wrong or missing span detail, LOW is extra or cosmetic.
- `trueup.core.adapters`: one data-driven adapter per library saying where it keeps tokens, finish reasons, outputs and response ids. Tested against span JSON from the sweeps, saved in `tests/fixtures/spans/` with stack traces and local URLs removed. OpenLLMetry error spans for failed Responses streams have no `gen_ai.operation.name`, so its adapter keys on `gen_ai.provider.name`.
- Choices made while comparing: finish reasons are compared through a synonym table (end_turn = stop, tool_use = tool_calls = tool_call, incomplete = length), because OpenLLMetry normalises them; a completed Responses call that asked for a tool may show `tool_call`. When the app closes a stream early, output, tokens and finish are not compared, since the app never got them. Tokens are only compared when the fake sent usage. Spans are matched to calls by response id, then by start order.
- A mismatch is called a lead. `trueup sweep <lib>` now prints a leads table, writes `leads.json` and exits 1 if there is any lead.
- `trueup audit <agent.py> --library <lib>` runs the script's `main()` against the fake, once per fake scenario on each route the script calls, and compares. Limits are written in `src/trueup/audit.py`. Tried on `examples/agent.py` under openinference: 8 runs, 1 lead (refusal not recorded).

Sweeps after the comparer (31/31 ran for each library). These are leads, not confirmed bugs; the self-check comes next.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 22 | 4 | 18 | 0 | 5 |
| openinference | 10 | 2 | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| openllmetry | 14 | 11 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

Leads per check:

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 | 4 |
| tokens | 3 | 0 | 4 |
| output | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| finish | 10 | 7 | 0 |

- neatlogs: Anthropic `messages.stream` spans carry no tokens, text, tool calls or finish reason (3 scenarios); Responses spans carry no status/finish (7) and no function calls (2); the chat refusal is not recorded; the Responses stream that ends with an error event stays UNSET with no exception event. The 5 notes are neatlogs adding `stream_options.include_usage` to streamed chat requests; tokens were compared against what the fake really sent.
- openinference: no span for a chat stream closed early or for a Responses stream ending in an error event; Responses spans carry no status/finish (7); the chat refusal is not recorded.
- openllmetry: chat streams that raised (error event, cut) and the Responses error-event stream end OK; no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream error/cut; Anthropic streamed spans record 4 output tokens where the provider sent 3 (4 scenarios).

## 2026-10-10: framework scenarios

- The fake now runs agent flows. It picks each reply from the request, so it keeps no state: no tool result yet means a tool call, a tool result means the answer. Chat Completions: one tool, two parallel tools, a loop that always asks for the tool, and HTTP 500 on the second call. Responses (for the OpenAI Agents SDK): one tool, a loop, 500 on the second call, a tool name the agent does not have, and an error event or a dropped connection in the streamed answer, after the full streamed event sequence of the first call. Fixture tests run them through the real openai SDK, LangChain, LangGraph and the Agents SDK.
- 20 framework scenarios are built: LangChain 6, LangGraph 6, OpenAI Agents SDK 8. Each has expected truth, including which tools really ran and which raised. The untraced check runs all 51 scenarios with the real SDKs. Two things it showed: LangGraph's `create_react_agent` does not raise at the step limit (it answers "Sorry, need more steps"), and langchain-openai raises its own `OpenAIAPIError` and `OpenAIConnectionError`.
- Setups per framework. neatlogs: `neatlogs.init(instrumentations=[...])` with its README keys (`langchain`, `langchain`+`langgraph`, `openai_agents`), export off. OpenInference: `LangChainInstrumentor` or `OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor`, and the OpenAI/Anthropic ones only for plain SDK runs. OpenLLMetry: `Traceloop.init(exporter=<in-memory>, disable_batch=True)` for everything. The Agents SDK's own uploader to api.openai.com is removed; the instrumentors' processors stay. Each agent gets its own AsyncOpenAI client.
- Trap found: the first neatlogs LangChain run exported no spans and raised no error. neatlogs checks `import langchain`, and the venv had `langchain-core` and `langchain-openai` but not `langchain`, so it logged "Skipped: langchain (not installed)". Every venv now installs `langchain`. Before a framework scenario runs, the runner checks that the framework imports and that an instrumentor for it is active, and reports NOT RUN with the reason if not. A regression test covers this.
- Comparer: run status uses the trace root (for the Agents SDK, "Agent workflow"). Two new checks. `tools`: every tool that really ran has a tool span, and a tool that raised has an ERROR span or an exception event. `error_recorded`: when the app raised but no provider call failed (unknown tool, max turns), some span must record an error. The OpenLLMetry adapter no longer counts LangGraph task, tool, agent and workflow spans as LLM calls. A scenario can say the app itself asked for stream usage, so LangChain's `stream_usage=True` is not reported as the library changing the request.

Sweeps with all 51 scenarios (runs `20261010T203332Z-neatlogs`, `20261010T203600Z-openinference`, `20261010T203755Z-openllmetry`). 51/51 ran for each library; nothing NOT RUN. The plain-SDK counts are unchanged from the last sweep. These are leads, not confirmed bugs.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes | of which framework |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 58 | 9 | 49 | 0 | 5 | 36 (high 5, medium 31) |
| openinference | 19 | 7 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 9 (high 5, medium 4) |
| openllmetry | 29 | 21 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 15 (high 10, medium 5) |

Leads per check (all scenarios; framework scenarios in brackets):

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 6 (5) | 5 (5) | 8 (5) |
| call_status | 4 (3) | 3 (3) | 6 (3) |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 5 (5) |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 (0) | 4 (0) |
| tokens | 3 (0) | 0 | 4 (0) |
| output | 8 (1) | 2 (1) | 1 (1) |
| finish | 37 (27) | 7 (0) | 0 |
| tools | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| error_recorded | 0 | 0 | 1 (1) |

- All three: when an Agents SDK run raises (500 on the second call, max turns, unknown tool, streamed error event, streamed cut), the root "Agent workflow" span is OK (5 scenarios each). For the provider failures the inner `response` span is ERROR but has no exception event (3 each). The LangChain refusal is not recorded as output (1 each). Tool spans were right everywhere, including the raised tool.
- neatlogs: framework LLM spans have no `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` (27). The OpenInference `llm.finish_reason` is on the same span; the adapter reads the neatlogs namespace only, as in the plain-SDK sweeps.
- openllmetry: in non-streamed Agents SDK runs every model call gets two LLM spans, one from the Agents SDK instrumentation and one from the OpenAI instrumentation under it. That doubles calls and tokens (ag-run: 2 calls and 36 tokens really; 4 spans and 72 tokens in the trace). Streamed runs get one span per call. The unknown-tool error is on no span: `no_such_tool` only appears as the tool call in the model's output.

Answers to the three questions:
1. Does a crashed Agents SDK run show OK at the top level? Yes, in all three libraries, in all 5 crash scenarios.
2. Does OpenLLMetry with Traceloop.init double LLM calls and tokens for the Agents SDK? Yes in non-streamed runs (5 of 5 scenarios, exactly 2x). Streamed runs are not affected (3 of 3 have one span per call and the right tokens).
3. Does an unknown-tool error appear anywhere in the trace? neatlogs and OpenInference: only as the status description of the `turn` span (ERROR, no exception event); the root stays OK. OpenLLMetry: nowhere.
# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Framework scenarios: 20 built (LangChain 6, LangGraph 6, OpenAI Agents SDK 8), each with expected truth, including which tools ran and which raised. App code in `trueup.runner.framework_apps`.
- Fake provider: agent flows on Chat Completions and Responses. Tool call then answer, parallel tools, a tool loop, 500 on the second call, an unknown tool name, and an error event or a cut in the second streamed call.
- Runner: each library's setup per framework. neatlogs uses its README keys, OpenInference its LangChain and OpenAI Agents instrumentors, OpenLLMetry `Traceloop.init`. The framework packages, `langchain` included, are installed in every venv. A framework scenario is NOT RUN, with the reason, if the framework does not import or no instrumentor for it is active. The Agents SDK's own trace upload is turned off.
- Comparer: run status uses the trace root. New `tools` and `error_recorded` checks. OpenLLMetry framework spans (agent, task, tool, workflow) are no longer counted as LLM calls. A scenario can say the app asked for stream usage itself.
- `trueup sweep <library> --framework all|none|langchain|openai-agents`. The default is all.
- Dev dependencies: `langchain-openai`, `langgraph`, `openai-agents`.

- Comparer (`trueup.core.compare`): checks run status, call status, call count, span closed, tokens, output and finish, with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW severity. Records a library changing the request (such as adding `stream_options.include_usage`) as a LOW note.
- Adapters (`trueup.core.adapters`): one per library for neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry, tested on saved span JSON in `tests/fixtures/spans/`.
- Reports (`trueup.core.report`): leads table and `leads.json`.
- `trueup sweep <library>` compares, prints the leads table, writes `leads.json`, and exits 1 if there is any lead.
- `trueup audit <script> --library <library>`: runs the script's `main()` against the fake through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, once per fake scenario on each route it calls, and compares. Example script in `examples/agent.py`.
- The fake provider can be told which scenario to answer with on a route, whatever the model name.
- `Mismatch` has `check` and `kind` ("lead" or "note").
- Fake provider (`trueup.fake`) for OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages, with a truth log.
- Scenario library (`trueup.scenarios`): 31 plain-SDK scenarios; framework scenarios listed as not built.
- Runner (`trueup.runner`): one scenario per subprocess in a per-library uv venv (neatlogs, openinference, openllmetry), spans captured in memory.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`.
- Dev dependencies: `openai`, `anthropic`. Tests that spawn subprocesses are marked `e2e` and excluded by default.
- Project skeleton: uv project, `trueup` command, data model in `trueup.core`, `doctor` command, tests and CI.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any


class Severity(Enum):
    HIGH = "high"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    LOW = "low"

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        # Higher rank means more severe.
        return {"high": 3, "medium": 2, "low": 1}[self.value]

    def __lt__(self, other: Severity) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Severity):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.rank < other.rank

    def __le__(self, other: Severity) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Severity):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.rank <= other.rank

    def __gt__(self, other: Severity) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Severity):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.rank > other.rank

    def __ge__(self, other: Severity) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Severity):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.rank >= other.rank


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Observation:
    """What really happened (truth) next to what the trace recorded (trace)."""

    truth: dict[str, Any]
    trace: dict[str, Any]

        return {"truth": dict(self.truth), "trace": dict(self.trace)}

        return cls(truth=dict(d["truth"]), trace=dict(d["trace"]))

"""Where each tracing library keeps the facts the comparer needs. Pure, data-driven.

One Adapter per library. Each names the attribute keys (or key patterns) for:
which spans are LLM calls, tokens, finish reasons, output text, refusals and
tool calls. Two shapes exist: flat attributes with numeric indexes
(neatlogs, OpenInference) and one JSON attribute holding the output messages
(OpenLLMetry's gen_ai.output.messages).

Adding a library means adding one Adapter here, not changing the comparer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

# Finish reasons with the same meaning, mapped to one name. OpenLLMetry
# normalises to the OTel GenAI names (stop, tool_call, length); the providers
# and the other libraries keep the raw ones.
FINISH_SYNONYMS = {
    "end_turn": "stop",
    "stop_sequence": "stop",
    "completed": "stop",
    "tool_calls": "tool_call",
    "tool_use": "tool_call",
    "function_call": "tool_call",
    "max_tokens": "length",
    "incomplete": "length",
}


def norm_finish(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    return None if value is None else FINISH_SYNONYMS.get(value, value)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Adapter:
    library: str
    # A span is an LLM call if attributes[key] is in values (any value if values is empty)
    # and no llm_exclude rule matches (same shape).
    llm_kind: tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]
    input_tokens: tuple[str, ...]
    output_tokens: tuple[str, ...]
    response_id: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # Keys whose value is one finish reason or a list of them; regexes match indexed keys.
    finish: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # Flat shape: regexes over attribute keys. Tool name/arguments regexes have
    # one group per index, used to pair a name with its arguments.
    text: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    refusal: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    tool_name: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    tool_args: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # JSON shape: one attribute with a list of {"parts": [{"type", "content"|"name"|"arguments"}]}.
    messages_json: str | None = None
    llm_exclude: tuple[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], ...] = ()
    # Tool spans (framework runs): same rule shape as llm_kind, and where the tool name is.
    tool_kind: tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]] | None = None
    tool_span_name: tuple[str, ...] = ()


NEATLOGS = Adapter(
    library="neatlogs",
    llm_kind=("neatlogs.span.kind", ("llm",)),
    input_tokens=("neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt",),
    output_tokens=("neatlogs.llm.token_count.completion",),
    response_id=("neatlogs.llm.response_id",),
    finish=(r"neatlogs\.llm\.finish_reason", r"neatlogs\.llm\.choices\.\d+\.finish_reason"),
    text=(r"neatlogs\.llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.content",),
    refusal=(r"neatlogs\.llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.refusal",),
    tool_name=(r"neatlogs\.llm\.tool_calls\.(\d+)\.name",),
    tool_args=(r"neatlogs\.llm\.tool_calls\.(\d+)\.arguments",),
    tool_kind=("neatlogs.span.kind", ("tool",)),
    tool_span_name=("neatlogs.tool.name", "tool.name"),
)

OPENINFERENCE = Adapter(
    library="openinference",
    llm_kind=("openinference.span.kind", ("LLM",)),
    input_tokens=("llm.token_count.prompt",),
    output_tokens=("llm.token_count.completion",),
    finish=(r"llm\.finish_reason",),
    text=(
        r"llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.message\.content",
        r"llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.message\.contents\.\d+\.message_content\.text",
    ),
    refusal=(r"llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.message\.refusal",),
    tool_name=(r"llm\.output_messages\.(\d+\.message\.tool_calls\.\d+)\.tool_call\.function\.name",),
    tool_args=(r"llm\.output_messages\.(\d+\.message\.tool_calls\.\d+)\.tool_call\.function\.arguments",),
    tool_kind=("openinference.span.kind", ("TOOL",)),
    tool_span_name=("tool.name",),
)

OPENLLMETRY = Adapter(
    library="openllmetry",
    # Error spans for failed streams carry no gen_ai.operation.name, so key on the provider.
    # Framework spans carry a provider too (langgraph, openai): agent, task, tool and workflow
    # spans are told apart by their operation name or traceloop.span.kind.
    llm_kind=("gen_ai.provider.name", ()),
    llm_exclude=(
        ("gen_ai.operation.name", ("create_agent", "invoke_agent", "execute_task", "execute_tool")),
        ("traceloop.span.kind", ()),
    ),
    tool_kind=("traceloop.span.kind", ("tool",)),
    tool_span_name=("gen_ai.tool.name",),
    input_tokens=("gen_ai.usage.input_tokens",),
    output_tokens=("gen_ai.usage.output_tokens",),
    response_id=("gen_ai.response.id",),
    finish=(r"gen_ai\.response\.finish_reasons",),
    messages_json="gen_ai.output.messages",
)

ADAPTERS: dict[str, Adapter] = {a.library: a for a in (NEATLOGS, OPENINFERENCE, OPENLLMETRY)}

# Reasoning text is not output text. OpenInference marks it per content part.
_OI_REASONING = re.compile(r"(llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.message\.contents\.\d+)\.message_content\.text")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SpanFacts:
    """What one LLM span says, in the comparer's terms."""

    input_tokens: int | None
    output_tokens: int | None
    response_id: str | None
    finish: tuple[str, ...]
    texts: tuple[str, ...]
    refusals: tuple[str, ...]
    tool_calls: tuple[tuple[str, Any], ...]  # (name, arguments as recorded)


def _first(attrs: dict[str, Any], keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> Any:
    for k in keys:
        if attrs.get(k) is not None:
            return attrs[k]
    return None


def _matching(attrs: dict[str, Any], patterns: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[tuple[re.Match[str], Any]]:
    out = []
    for p in patterns:
        rx = re.compile(p)
        out += [(m, v) for k, v in attrs.items() if (m := rx.fullmatch(k))]
    return out


def _int(v: Any) -> int | None:
    try:
        return int(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _rule(rule: tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    key, values = rule
    v = attrs.get(key)
    return v is not None and (not values or v in values)


def is_llm_span(adapter: Adapter, span: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    attrs = span.get("attributes", {})
    return _rule(adapter.llm_kind, attrs) and not any(_rule(r, attrs) for r in adapter.llm_exclude)


def tool_span_name(adapter: Adapter, span: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """The tool's name if this is a tool span, else None."""
    attrs = span.get("attributes", {})
    if adapter.tool_kind is None or not _rule(adapter.tool_kind, attrs):
        return None
    name = _first(attrs, adapter.tool_span_name)
    return name if isinstance(name, str) else span.get("name")


def _flat_outputs(adapter: Adapter, attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[tuple[str, Any]]]:
    texts = []
    for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.text):
        rm = _OI_REASONING.fullmatch(m.group(0))
        if rm and attrs.get(f"{rm.group(1)}.message_content.type") == "reasoning":
            continue
        if isinstance(v, str):
            texts.append(v)
    refusals = [v for _, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.refusal) if isinstance(v, str)]
    args = {m.group(1): v for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.tool_args)}
    tools = [(v, args.get(m.group(1))) for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.tool_name)]
    return texts, refusals, tools


def _json_outputs(raw: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[tuple[str, Any]]]:
    texts: list[str] = []
    refusals: list[str] = []
    tools: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
    try:
        messages = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else (raw or [])
    except ValueError:
        return texts, refusals, tools
    for msg in messages if isinstance(messages, list) else []:
        for part in (msg or {}).get("parts", []) if isinstance(msg, dict) else []:
            kind = part.get("type")
            if kind == "text" and isinstance(part.get("content"), str):
                texts.append(part["content"])
            elif kind == "refusal" and isinstance(part.get("content"), str):
                refusals.append(part["content"])
            elif kind == "tool_call":
                tools.append((part.get("name"), part.get("arguments")))
    return texts, refusals, tools


def _finish(adapter: Adapter, attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for _, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.finish):
        for x in v if isinstance(v, list) else [v]:
            if isinstance(x, str) and x:
                out.append(x)
    return tuple(out)


def facts(adapter: Adapter, span: dict[str, Any]) -> SpanFacts:
    attrs = span.get("attributes", {})
    if adapter.messages_json:
        texts, refusals, tools = _json_outputs(attrs.get(adapter.messages_json))
    else:
        texts, refusals, tools = _flat_outputs(adapter, attrs)
    rid = _first(attrs, adapter.response_id)
    return SpanFacts(
        input_tokens=_int(_first(attrs, adapter.input_tokens)),
        output_tokens=_int(_first(attrs, adapter.output_tokens)),
        response_id=rid if isinstance(rid, str) else None,
        finish=_finish(adapter, attrs),
        texts=tuple(texts),
        refusals=tuple(refusals),
        tool_calls=tuple(tools),
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from trueup.runner.setups import LIBRARIES

# Exit codes
EXIT_OK = 0  # no mismatches
EXIT_MISMATCH = 1  # mismatches found
EXIT_ERROR = 2  # could not run

KEY_VARS = ("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY")
NOT_BUILT = ("fix", "upstream", "verify", "report")


def doctor() -> int:
    ok = sys.version_info >= (3, 12)
    v = sys.version_info
    print(f"python: {v.major}.{v.minor}.{v.micro} ({'ok' if ok else 'need 3.12+'})")
    for name in KEY_VARS:
        # Only report presence. Never print the value.
        state = "set" if os.environ.get(name) else "not set"
        print(f"{name}: {state}")
    return EXIT_OK if ok else EXIT_ERROR


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="trueup",
        description="Find where AI agent traces disagree with what really happened.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in NOT_BUILT:
        sub.add_parser(name, help="not built yet")
    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="check the local setup")
    sw = sub.add_parser("sweep", help="run the scenarios against one tracing library")
    sw.add_argument("library", choices=LIBRARIES)
    sw.add_argument("--framework", default="all", choices=("all", "none", "langchain", "openai-agents"),
                    help="none: plain SDK; langchain: LangChain and LangGraph; default all")
    au = sub.add_parser("audit", help="run your script's main() against the fake provider and compare its trace")
    au.add_argument("script", type=Path, help="Python file with a main() that calls the openai or anthropic SDK")
    au.add_argument("--library", required=True, choices=LIBRARIES, help="tracing library to set up")
    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "doctor":
        return doctor()
    if args.command == "sweep":
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code, sweep

        _, results = sweep(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.framework)
        return exit_code(results)
    if args.command == "audit":
        from trueup.audit import audit
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code

        _, results = audit(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.script)
        return exit_code(results)
    print(f"trueup {args.command}: not built yet", file=sys.stderr)
    return EXIT_ERROR


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.core import report
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Observation
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run
from trueup.scenarios import select


def new_run_id(library: str) -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + f"-{library}"


def summary_line(r: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    sid = r["scenario"]
    if r["status"] != RAN:
        return f"{sid:30} NOT RUN  {r['reason']}"
    t, tr = r["observation"]["truth"], r["observation"]["trace"]
    app = t["app"]["outcome"] if t["outcome"] == "ok" else f"raised {t['exception']}"
    spans = ", ".join(f"{s['name']}={s['status']['code']}" for s in tr["spans"]) or "none"
    line = f"{sid:30} ran {r['seconds']:5.1f}s  app {app}; fake calls {t['calls']}; spans {len(tr['spans'])}: {spans}"
    if t.get("expected_mismatch"):
        line += f"  [truth differs from scenario expectation: {', '.join(t['expected_mismatch'])}]"
    return line


def sweep(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    framework: str = "all",
    *,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library)
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = time.monotonic()
    scenarios = select(framework)
    try:
        out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
        python: Path | None = ensure(root, library)
        venv_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every scenario is reported NOT RUN
        python, venv_error = None, f"venv not ready: {e}"
    results = []
    for s in scenarios:
        r = not_run(s.id, library, venv_error) if python is None else run(python, library, s.id)
        if r["status"] == RAN:
            r["mismatches"] = [m.to_dict() for m in compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"]))]
        results.append(r)
        out(summary_line(r))
        (run_dir / f"{s.id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
    ran = sum(r["status"] == RAN for r in results)
    by = by_scenario(results)
    c = report.counts(by)
    table = report.table(by)
    totals = (f"leads: {c['leads']} (high {c['by_severity']['high']}, medium {c['by_severity']['medium']}, "
              f"low {c['by_severity']['low']})  notes: {c['notes']}")
    lines = [
        f"trueup sweep {library} --framework {framework}  run {run_id}",
        f"scenarios: {len(results)}  ran: {ran}  not run: {len(results) - ran}  "
        f"time: {time.monotonic() - started:.0f} s",
        totals,
        "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace, not a confirmed bug.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
        "",
        table,
    ]
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (run_dir / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "framework": framework,
        "scenarios": [{"id": r["scenario"], "status": r["status"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results],
    }, indent=1))
    not_run_list = [{"scenario": r["scenario"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results if r["status"] != RAN]
    (run_dir / "leads.json").write_text(json.dumps(report.leads_payload(run_id, library, by, not_run_list), indent=1,
                                                   default=str))
    out("")
    out(table)
    out(totals)
    out(f"ran {ran}/{len(results)}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def by_scenario(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]:
    return [(r["scenario"], [Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])
            for r in results if r["status"] == RAN]


def exit_code(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """1 if any lead, else 2 if any scenario could not run, else 0."""
    if any(leads([m for _, ms in by_scenario(results) for m in ms])):
        return 1
    return 2 if not results or any(r["status"] == NOT_RUN for r in results) else 0

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from typing import Any

from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Severity

COLUMNS = ("scenario", "check", "expected", "actual", "severity")
CELL_MAX = 48


def _cell(v: Any) -> str:
    s = v if isinstance(v, str) else json.dumps(v, default=str)
    return s if len(s) <= CELL_MAX else s[: CELL_MAX - 3] + "..."


def rows(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> list[tuple[str, ...]]:
    out = []
    for sid, ms in by_scenario:
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda m: -m.severity.rank):
            check = m.check if m.kind == "lead" else f"{m.check} (note)"
            out.append((sid, check, _cell(m.truth), _cell(m.trace), m.severity.value.upper()))
    return out


def table(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> str:
    body = rows(by_scenario)
    if not body:
        return "no leads"
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in [COLUMNS, *body]) for i in range(len(COLUMNS))]
    line = lambda r: "  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r, widths)).rstrip()  # noqa: E731
    return "\n".join([line(COLUMNS), line(tuple("-" * w for w in widths)), *(line(r) for r in body)])


def counts(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    leads = [m for _, ms in by_scenario for m in ms if m.kind == "lead"]
    notes = [m for _, ms in by_scenario for m in ms if m.kind == "note"]
    sev = Counter(m.severity.value for m in leads)
    return {
        "leads": len(leads),
        "notes": len(notes),
        "by_severity": {s.value: sev.get(s.value, 0) for s in sorted(Severity, reverse=True)},
        "by_check": dict(sorted(Counter(m.check for m in leads).items())),
        "scenarios_with_leads": sum(any(m.kind == "lead" for m in ms) for _, ms in by_scenario),
    }


def leads_payload(run_id: str, library: str, by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]],
                  not_run: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "note": "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace. It is not a confirmed bug.",
        "counts": counts(by_scenario),
        "not_run": not_run,
        "scenarios": [{"scenario": sid, "mismatches": [m.to_dict() for m in ms]} for sid, ms in by_scenario],
    }

class FrameworkNotTraced(RuntimeError):
    """The framework or its instrumentation is missing, so the run would trace nothing."""


def _all_subclasses(cls: type) -> list[type]:
    out = []
    for sub in cls.__subclasses__():
        out += [sub, *_all_subclasses(sub)]
    return out


def active_instrumentors() -> list[str]:
    """Module paths of OTel instrumentors that are instrumented right now (they are singletons)."""
    try:
        from opentelemetry.instrumentation.instrumentor import BaseInstrumentor
    except ImportError:
        return []
    return sorted({
        f"{c.__module__}.{c.__name__}"
        for c in _all_subclasses(BaseInstrumentor)
        if getattr(c.__dict__.get("_instance"), "_is_instrumented_by_opentelemetry", False)
    })


def check_framework(framework: str, active: Callable[[], list[str]] = active_instrumentors) -> None:
    """Raise FrameworkNotTraced unless the framework imports and an instrumentor for it is active."""
    if framework == "none":
        return
    for module in FRAMEWORK_MODULES[framework]:
        try:
            importlib.import_module(module)
        except ImportError as e:
            raise FrameworkNotTraced(f"{framework}: cannot import {module} ({e}); its instrumentation would do nothing") from None
    token = FRAMEWORK_INSTRUMENTOR[framework]
    names = active()
    if not any(token in n for n in names):
        raise FrameworkNotTraced(f"{framework}: no active instrumentor with {token!r} in its module; "
                                 f"active: {', '.join(names) or 'none'}")

    return {

        "langchain": ["langchain"],
        "langgraph": ["langchain", "langgraph"],
        "openai-agents": ["openai_agents"],

    """Drop the Agents SDK's own trace uploader (it posts to api.openai.com). Instrumentor processors stay."""
    try:

        from agents.tracing.processors import default_processor
    except ImportError:

    multi = getattr(get_trace_provider(), "_multi_processor", None)
    if multi is not None:
        multi.set_processors([p for p in multi._processors if p is not default_processor()])

        "instrumentations": neatlogs_instrumentations(framework),

def setup_neatlogs(framework: str = "none"):
    import neatlogs
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    neatlogs.init(**neatlogs_init_kwargs(provider, framework))
    # Added after init so we see spans after neatlogs' own processor ran.
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))

    def flush() -> None:
        neatlogs.flush(timeout_millis=5000)
        provider.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush


def setup_openinference(framework: str = "none"):
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
    # The framework's instrumentor alone, as its docs show; the SDK ones for plain SDK use.
    if framework in ("langchain", "langgraph"):
        from openinference.instrumentation.langchain import LangChainInstrumentor

        LangChainInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    elif framework == "openai-agents":
        from openinference.instrumentation.openai_agents import OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor

        OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    else:
        from openinference.instrumentation.anthropic import AnthropicInstrumentor
        from openinference.instrumentation.openai import OpenAIInstrumentor

        OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
        AnthropicInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    return exporter, lambda: provider.force_flush(5000)


def setup_openllmetry(framework: str = "none"):
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
    from traceloop.sdk import Traceloop

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    # Same call for every framework: Traceloop.init instruments whatever it can import.
    Traceloop.init(app_name="trueup", exporter=exporter, disable_batch=True, telemetry_enabled=False)

    def flush() -> None:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        p = trace.get_tracer_provider()
        if hasattr(p, "force_flush"):
            p.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush

This module gathers the evidence (the effects); the rules in trueup.core.checker

  2. rerun every scenario with a lead twice, each in a fresh process

  4. read the other libraries' latest sweeps of the same scenarios (compared again with
     today's adapters)
  5. generate a repro per scenario and run it
  6. apply the rules, group findings by cause, search GitHub for each finding (read only)
Writes findings.json, withdrawn.json and evidence.json next to the sweep's leads.json.

    "openllmetry": ("traceloop-sdk", *(f"opentelemetry-instrumentation-{n}" for n in ("openai", "anthropic",
                                                                                         "langchain", "openai-agents"))),

def find_run(root: Path, run_id: str, library: str | None) -> Path:
    runs = root / ".trueup" / "runs"
    if run_id != "latest":
        d = runs / run_id
        if not (d / "leads.json").exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no leads.json in {d}")
        return d
    cands = sorted(d for d in runs.glob("*") if (d / "leads.json").exists() and "-audit-" not in d.name

def run_repro(python: Path, path: Path, timeout: float = 120) -> dict[str, Any]:
    text = path.read_text()
    rec: dict[str, Any] = {"path": str(path), "lines": repro.line_count(text)}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-repro-") as tmp:
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([str(python), str(path)], env=child_env(), cwd=tmp, capture_output=True,
                               text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {**rec, "status": "not_run", "reason": f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s"}
    if p.returncode != 0:
        tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout).strip().splitlines()
        return {**rec, "status": "not_run", "reason": f"exit {p.returncode}: {tail[-1] if tail else ''}"}
    found = []
    for line in p.stdout.splitlines():
        try:
            found.append(checker.signature(json.loads(line)))
        except (ValueError, KeyError):
            continue
    return {**rec, "status": "ran", "exit": p.returncode, "leads": found}


def gather(root: Path, run_dir: Path, library: str, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
           run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Evidence per lead in the sweep."""
    payload = json.loads((run_dir / "leads.json").read_text())
    by_scenario: dict[str, tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]] = {}
    for s in payload["scenarios"]:
        r = json.loads((run_dir / f"{s['scenario']}.json").read_text())
        if r["status"] != RAN:
            continue
        # Compare again with today's adapters, so an adapter fix applies to old sweeps.
        ls = _lead_dicts(library, s["scenario"], compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"])))
        if ls:
            by_scenario[s["scenario"]] = (r["observation"], ls)
    total = sum(len(v[1]) for v in by_scenario.values())
    out(f"{library}: {total} leads in {len(by_scenario)} scenarios ({run_dir.name})")

    out("upgrading the venv to the latest release")
    py = venvs.upgrade(root, library)
    pypi = {d: pypi_latest(d) for d in LIB_DISTS[library]}
    out("building the main-branch venv")
    try:
        main_py, commit = venvs.ensure_main(root, library)
        main_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - recorded as "could not check"
        main_py, commit, main_error = None, "", f"could not install main: {e}"
    others = other_runs(root, library)
    harness = {"env": {k: v for k, v in child_env().items() if k in HARNESS_ENV}}
    repro_dir = run_dir / "repros"
    repro_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    evidence = []
    for sid, (obs, ls) in by_scenario.items():
        s = get(sid)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        reruns = [_run_record(run(py, library, sid), s.framework, library) for _ in range(2)]
        installed = (reruns[0].get("versions") or {}) if reruns else {}
        latest = {"installed": {d: installed.get(d) for d in LIB_DISTS[library] if installed.get(d)}, "pypi": pypi}
        if main_py is None:
            main = {"status": "could_not_install", "reason": main_error}
        else:
            m = _run_record(run(main_py, library, sid), s.framework, library)
            main = {**m, "commit": commit, "reason": m["reason"] and f"main run: {m['reason']}"}
        path = repro_dir / f"{library}-{sid}.py"
        path.write_text(repro.generate(library, sid, s.does))
        rp = run_repro(py, path)
        rp["path"] = str(path.relative_to(root.resolve()))
        oth = other_evidence(others, sid)
        scen = {"id": sid, "framework": s.framework, "provider": s.provider, "api": s.api, "app": s.app}
        for lead in ls:
            evidence.append({"lead": lead, "scenario": scen, "observation": obs, "reruns": reruns, "latest": latest,
                             "main": main, "harness": harness, "others": oth, "repro": rp})
        out(f"  {sid:28} {len(ls)} lead(s) checked in {time.monotonic() - t0:.0f} s")
    return evidence


def decide(evidence: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    items = []
    for ev in evidence:
        results = checker.run_rules(ev)
        status, by = checker.verdict(results)
        items.append({"lead": ev["lead"], "scenario": ev["scenario"], "status": status,
                      "rules": [r.to_dict() for r in results], "decided_by": by.to_dict() if by else None})
    return items


def check(root: Path, run_id: str, library: str | None, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
          search: Callable[[list[str]], str] = dedupe.gh_search) -> dict[str, Any]:
    run_dir = find_run(root, run_id, library)
    lib = json.loads((run_dir / "leads.json").read_text())["library"]
    if library and lib != library:
        raise ValueError(f"{run_dir.name} is a {lib} sweep, not {library}")
    evidence = gather(root, run_dir, lib, out)
    items = decide(evidence)
    checked_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")

    findings = group.group([i for i in items if i["status"] == checker.FINDING])
    out("searching GitHub issues and PRs (read only)")
    known = dedupe.dedupe(lib, findings, search)
    finding_dicts = [{**f.to_dict(), "dedupe": known[f.id]} for f in findings]
    disputed = [f.to_dict() for f in group.group([i for i in items if i["status"] == checker.DISPUTED_SEMANTICS])]
    open_leads = [i for i in items if i["status"] == checker.LEAD]
    withdrawn = [i for i in items if i["status"] == checker.WITHDRAWN]

    counts = {
        "leads": len(items),
        "finding_leads": sum(i["status"] == checker.FINDING for i in items),
        "findings": len(findings),
        "findings_by_severity": dict(Counter(f.severity.value for f in findings)),
        "disputed": len(disputed),
        "open_leads": len(open_leads),
        "withdrawn": len(withdrawn),
        "withdrawn_by_rule": dict(Counter(i["decided_by"]["rule"] for i in withdrawn)),
        "already_known": sum(k["status"] == "already known" for k in known.values()),
    }
    common = {"run_id": run_dir.name, "library": lib, "checked_at": checked_at}
    (run_dir / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        **common, "counts": counts, "findings": finding_dicts, "disputed_semantics": disputed,
        "open_leads": open_leads}, indent=1, default=str))
    (run_dir / "withdrawn.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        **common, "note": "Withdrawn leads are kept and counted, never deleted.", "withdrawn": withdrawn},
        indent=1, default=str))
    (run_dir / "evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        [{k: v for k, v in ev.items() if k != "observation"} for ev in evidence], indent=1, default=str))
    out(summary(lib, counts, finding_dicts))
    out(f"wrote {run_dir}/findings.json, withdrawn.json, evidence.json")
    return {"run_dir": run_dir, "counts": counts}


def summary(library: str, counts: dict[str, Any], findings: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    sev = counts["findings_by_severity"]
    lines = [
        f"{library}: {counts['leads']} leads -> {counts['findings']} findings "
        f"({counts['finding_leads']} leads), {counts['withdrawn']} withdrawn, "
        f"{counts['disputed']} disputed semantics, {counts['open_leads']} still leads",
        "",
        "findings by severity: " + ", ".join(f"{s} {sev.get(s, 0)}" for s in ("high", "medium", "low")),
        "withdrawn by rule:    " + (", ".join(f"{r} {n}" for r, n in sorted(counts["withdrawn_by_rule"].items()))
                                    or "none"),
        f"already known:        {counts['already_known']}",
        "",
    ]
    rows = [("severity", "scenarios", "known", "finding")]
    for f in findings:
        k = f["dedupe"]
        rows.append((f["severity"].upper(), str(len(f["details"]["scenarios"])),
                     k["links"][0] if k["status"] == "already known" else "-", f["title"]))
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in range(3)]
    lines += ["  ".join([*(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r[:3], widths)), r[3]]) for r in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Search a library's GitHub issues and PRs (all states) for each finding. Read only.

Uses `gh search issues --include-prs`. Never opens, comments on or posts anything.
For each finding it records the searches with their dates, the titles of the
integration's issues and PRs, and whether one of them already covers the
finding ("already known", with the link).

Queries and matching are pure (queries, matches); gh_search is the only effect.
A match needs the integration's name and the specific behaviour in the title, so
it errs on the side of "not found"; the recorded searches let a reader check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.core.model import Finding

REPOS = {"neatlogs": "neatlogs/neatlogs", "openinference": "Arize-ai/openinference",
         "openllmetry": "traceloop/openllmetry"}
FIELDS = "number,title,url,state,isPullRequest,createdAt"
PAUSE_S = 2.5  # GitHub allows 30 search requests a minute

# Integration names per code path (for search terms and title matching).
INTEGRATION = {
    "openai chat create": ("openai",), "openai chat stream": ("openai",),
    "openai responses create": ("responses",), "openai responses stream": ("responses",),
    "anthropic messages create": ("anthropic",), "anthropic messages stream": ("anthropic",),
    "langchain": ("langchain",), "langgraph": ("langgraph", "langchain"),
    "openai-agents": ("openai-agents", "openai agents", "agents sdk", "openai_agents"),
}
# Search words, and title phrases any of which counts as the same behaviour, per check.
BEHAVIOUR: dict[str, tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = {
    "run_status": ("span status error", ("status", "mark", "error status", "not set to error")),
    "call_status": ("exception event", ("exception", "record_exception", "status")),
    "span_closed": ("span not ended stream", ("not ended", "never ended", "not closed", "missing span", "no span",
                                              "span leak", "not exported", "unfinished")),
    "call_count": ("duplicate spans", ("duplicate", "double", "twice")),
    "tokens": ("token usage", ("token", "usage")),
    "finish": ("finish reason", ("finish reason", "finish_reason", "stop reason", "stop_reason", "status")),
    "output": ("output", ("output", "refusal", "tool call", "function call", "tool_calls")),
    "error_recorded": ("error not recorded", ("error",)),
    "tools": ("tool span", ("tool",)),
}


def queries(f: Finding) -> list[str]:
    path, check, field = f.details["code_path"], f.details["check"], f.details["field"]
    integ = INTEGRATION.get(path, (path,))[0]
    words = BEHAVIOUR.get(check, (check, ()))[0]
    if check == "output":
        words = "refusal" if "text" in field and _is_refusal(f) else ("tool calls" if "tool" in field else "output")
    stream = " stream" if path.endswith("stream") else ""
    return [f"{integ} {words}{stream}", words + stream]


def _is_refusal(f: Finding) -> bool:
    return any("refusal" in lead["scenario"] for lead in f.details.get("leads", []))


def matches(f: Finding, items: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Issues/PRs whose title names the integration and the behaviour."""
    path, check = f.details["code_path"], f.details["check"]
    integ = INTEGRATION.get(path, (path,))
    phrases = BEHAVIOUR.get(check, ("", (check,)))[1]
    if check == "output":
        phrases = ("refusal",) if _is_refusal(f) else (("tool call", "function call", "tool_calls")
                                                     if "tool" in f.details["field"] else ("output",))
    out = []
    for it in items:
        t = it.get("title", "").lower()
        if any(i in t for i in integ) and any(p in t for p in phrases):
            out.append(it)
    return out


def gh_search(args: list[str]) -> str:
    p = subprocess.run(["gh", "search", "issues", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError((p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-300:])
    return p.stdout


def _search(search: Callable[[list[str]], str], repo: str, query: str, limit: int,
            cache: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if query in cache:
        return cache[query]
    rec: dict[str, Any] = {"repo": repo, "query": query, "states": "all", "include_prs": True,
                           "date": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    try:
        rec["results"] = json.loads(search([query, "--repo", repo, "--include-prs", "--limit", str(limit),
                                            "--json", FIELDS]))
    except (RuntimeError, ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as e:
        rec["results"], rec["error"] = [], str(e)
    if search is gh_search:
        time.sleep(PAUSE_S)
    cache[query] = rec
    return rec


def dedupe(library: str, findings: list[Finding], search: Callable[[list[str]], str] = gh_search,
           ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    repo = REPOS[library]
    cache: dict[str, Any] = {}
    out = {}
    for f in findings:
        searches = [_search(search, repo, q, 30, cache) for q in queries(f)]
        integ = INTEGRATION.get(f.details["code_path"], (f.details["code_path"],))[0]
        listing = _search(search, repo, integ, 100, cache)
        seen: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for s in [*searches, listing]:
            for it in s["results"]:
                seen.setdefault(it["url"], it)
        hits = matches(f, list(seen.values()))
        out[f.id] = {
            "status": "already known" if hits else "not found",
            "links": [h["url"] for h in hits],
            "matched": [{"title": h["title"], "url": h["url"], "state": h["state"]} for h in hits],
            "searches": [{k: v for k, v in s.items() if k != "results"} | {"hits": len(s["results"])}
                         for s in searches],
            "integration_titles": {"query": integ, "date": listing["date"],
                                   "titles": [f"#{it['number']} {it['title']} ({it['state']})"
                                              for it in listing["results"]]},
            "errors": [s["error"] for s in [*searches, listing] if s.get("error")],
        }
    return out

"""Checker rules, verdict, grouping, repro text and dedupe matching. All pure, over recorded data."""

import copy
import json

import pytest

from trueup import dedupe
from trueup.cli import EXIT_ERROR, main
from trueup.core import checker, group, repro
from trueup.core.checker import COULD_NOT_CHECK, DISPUTED, FAIL, PASS

LEAD = {"scenario": "oa-resp-plain", "library": "neatlogs", "check": "finish", "field": "call 1 finish",
        "truth": ["completed"], "trace": None, "severity": "medium"}
SIG = checker.signature(LEAD)


def evidence(**over):
    ev = {
        "lead": dict(LEAD),
        "observation": {"truth": {"fake_log": [{"response_id": "resp-1", "usage_sent": True,
                                                "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 7},
                                                "scenario": "resp-plain"}],
                                  "expected_mismatch": [], "app": {"outcome": "ok"}}},
        "reruns": [{"status": "ran", "leads": [SIG], "versions": {"neatlogs": "1.0"}, "seconds": 3.0,
                    "framework": "none", "setup": "neatlogs.init"}] * 2,
        "latest": {"installed": {"neatlogs": "1.0"}, "pypi": {"neatlogs": "1.0"}},
        "main": {"status": "ran", "leads": [SIG], "commit": "abcdef1234567"},
        "harness": {"env": {"NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT": "true", "OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER": "none"}},
        "others": {"openllmetry": {"status": "ran", "leads": []}},
        "repro": {"status": "ran", "lines": 30, "leads": [SIG], "path": "r.py"},
    }
    ev.update(over)
    return ev


def test_all_rules_pass_is_a_finding():
    results = checker.run_rules(evidence())
    assert [r.status for r in results] == [PASS] * 7
    assert checker.verdict(results) == (checker.FINDING, None)


def test_fresh_process_needs_two_identical_reruns():
    other = [*SIG[:3], ["stop"]]
    ev = evidence(reruns=[evidence()["reruns"][0], {"status": "ran", "leads": [other], "seconds": 1}])
    r = checker.fresh_process(ev)
    assert r.status == FAIL and "rerun 2" in r.reason
    assert checker.fresh_process(evidence(reruns=[])).status == COULD_NOT_CHECK


def test_recommended_setup_needs_the_framework_installed():
    ev = evidence(reruns=[{"status": "ran", "framework": "langgraph", "versions": {"langchain-core": "1"}}] * 2)
    r = checker.recommended_setup(ev)
    assert r.status == FAIL and "langgraph" in r.reason


def test_latest_and_main():
    assert checker.latest_and_main(evidence(latest={"installed": {"neatlogs": "0.9"},
                                                    "pypi": {"neatlogs": "1.0"}})).status == FAIL
    fixed = checker.latest_and_main(evidence(main={"status": "ran", "leads": [], "commit": "abc"}))
    assert fixed.status == FAIL and "fixed" in fixed.reason
    cnc = checker.latest_and_main(evidence(main={"status": "could_not_install", "reason": "build failed"}))
    assert cnc.status == COULD_NOT_CHECK and "build failed" in cnc.reason


def test_main_not_checked_with_reason_and_rest_passing_is_a_finding():
    results = checker.run_rules(evidence(main={"status": "could_not_install", "reason": "build failed"}))
    status, by = checker.verdict(results)
    assert status == checker.FINDING and by.rule == "latest_and_main"
    results = checker.run_rules(evidence(main={"status": "could_not_install", "reason": "x"}, repro={}))
    assert checker.verdict(results)[0] == checker.LEAD


def test_fake_truthful():
    ev = evidence()
    ev["observation"]["truth"]["fake_log"] = [{"response_id": "a"}, {"response_id": "a"}]
    assert checker.fake_truthful(ev).status == FAIL
    tok = evidence(lead={**LEAD, "check": "tokens", "field": "call 1 tokens"})
    assert checker.fake_truthful(tok).status == PASS
    tok["observation"]["truth"]["fake_log"][0]["usage_sent"] = False
    r = checker.fake_truthful(tok)
    assert r.status == FAIL and "no usage" in r.reason


def test_harness_sane():
    ev = evidence()
    ev["observation"] = copy.deepcopy(ev["observation"])
    ev["observation"]["truth"]["app"] = {"outcome": "exception", "message": "Event loop is closed"}
    assert checker.harness_sane(ev).status == FAIL
    dead = evidence(harness={"env": {"NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT": "true", "OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER": "none",
                                      "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:1"}})
    assert checker.harness_sane(dead).status == FAIL
    slow = evidence(reruns=[{**evidence()["reruns"][0], "seconds": 200}] * 2)
    assert checker.harness_sane(slow).status == FAIL


def test_reference_other_library_semconv_or_disputed():
    assert "openllmetry" in checker.reference(evidence()).reason
    agree = {"openllmetry": {"status": "ran", "leads": [SIG]}}
    assert checker.reference(evidence(others=agree)).reason.startswith("OTel GenAI")
    exc = {**LEAD, "check": "call_status", "field": "call 1 span status", "trace": "ERROR, no exception event"}
    r = checker.reference(evidence(lead=exc, others={"openllmetry": {"status": "ran",
                                                                     "leads": [checker.signature(exc)]}}))
    assert r.status == DISPUTED
    assert checker.verdict(checker.run_rules(evidence(lead=exc, others={"x": {"status": "ran", "leads": [
        checker.signature(exc)]}}, reruns=[{**evidence()["reruns"][0], "leads": [checker.signature(exc)]}] * 2,
        repro={"status": "ran", "lines": 30, "leads": [checker.signature(exc)]})))[0] == checker.DISPUTED_SEMANTICS


def test_refusal_has_no_semconv_reference():
    ev = evidence(lead={**LEAD, "check": "output", "field": "call 1 output text", "truth": "no"})
    ev["observation"]["truth"]["fake_log"][0]["scenario"] = "chat-refusal"
    assert checker.semconv_reference(ev["lead"], ev["observation"]["truth"]["fake_log"]) is None


def test_repro_rule():
    assert checker.repro(evidence(repro={"status": "ran", "lines": 45, "leads": [SIG]})).status == FAIL
    assert checker.repro(evidence(repro={"status": "ran", "lines": 30, "leads": []})).status == FAIL
    assert checker.repro(evidence(repro={"status": "not_run", "reason": "exit 1"})).status == COULD_NOT_CHECK


def test_withdrawn_names_the_first_failing_rule():
    status, by = checker.verdict(checker.run_rules(evidence(reruns=[])))

**Withdrawn by rule:** only `latest_and_main`, 2 leads (openllmetry `oa-resp-failed` and `oa-resp-incomplete`). They reproduce on 0.62.4 but not on main, so they are fixed there.
